title: Postmortem: 17 March 2026 - AlgoWorks Fleet API outage (Sev1)
body:
**Status:** Final | **Author:** Rohan Mehta | **Reviewers:** Varun Chandra, Arjun Venkataraman | **Incident ticket:** INC-21632

## Summary
On 17 March 2026 between 14:05 and 14:52 IST, approximately 60% of requests to the AlgoWorks Fleet API failed with 5xx errors. The customer portal showed errors and driver app check-ins were queued offline. 38 customers were affected. The cause was a configuration change in algoworks-api-gateway 4.2.0 that reduced the PgBouncer pool size per pod from 200 to 50; under production concurrency this exhausted available connections to RDS. Service was restored by rolling back to 4.1.7 via ArgoCD.

## Timeline (IST)
- 14:05 ArgoCD syncs algoworks-api-gateway 4.2.0 (merged PR #2231, GitOps approval by Priya Shah and Sneha Kulkarni).
- 14:07 First 5xx errors; RDS connection count reaches pool ceiling.
- 14:12 PagerDuty alert 'API 5xx rate > 5%'.
- 14:18 Sev1 declared, IC Varun Chandra.
- 14:24 Correlation with 4.2.0 pool-size change.
- 14:40 Rollback initiated.
- 14:52 Error rate below 1%.
- 15:00 Resolved. 15:30 Customer comms sent.
- 19-Mar Kinesis consumer lag from the rollback cleared (RITM-21647).

## Root cause
PR #2231 (v4 connection-management work) changed `default_pool_size` from 200 to 50 per pod to reduce idle connections, based on staging measurements. Staging runs ~40 concurrent sessions versus ~900 at production peak. The change was one of 40 files in the PR and was not called out in the description.

## What went well
- Correlation to the deploy in under 20 minutes; rollback in 35.
- ArgoCD rollback worked first time.
- Customer comms within 30 minutes of resolution.

## What went badly
- No alert on RDS connection utilisation.
- Staging load profile is not representative.
- High-risk config change hidden in a large PR.

## Action items
| # | Action | Owner | Due | Jira |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Datadog monitor: RDS connections > 80% of max pages Platform on-call | Sneha Kulkarni | 24-Mar | PLAT-2201 |
| 2 | Staging load test at >= 50% of prod peak as a required check for gateway deploys | Karthik Iyer | 30-Apr | PLAT-2205 |
| 3 | PR label `high-risk-config` required for pool/limit/timeout changes; must be a separate PR | Priya Shah | 31-Mar | PLAT-2206 |
| 4 | Dead-letter path for poison Kinesis records | Harish Gowda | 30-Apr | PLAT-2210 |
| 5 | CAB to decide whether config-only production changes need a CHG in addition to GitOps approval | Varun Chandra | 15-Apr | - |

_Blameless postmortem per the Incident Management & Severity Classification SOP._

title: Runbook: GitHub Actions self-hosted runners
body:
**Owner:** Cloud Infrastructure & Security | **Last updated:** 12 June 2026 (Siddharth Jain) | **Related:** INC-22029, CHG-22032

## Overview
Four self-hosted runners (runner-prod-1..4, c6i.2xlarge, ap-south-1) execute workflows that need VPC access (integration tests against staging RDS, ECR pushes, ArgoCD promotion). GitHub-hosted runners are used for everything else.

## Health checks
- Org settings > Actions > Runners: all four should be Idle/Active.
- Datadog dashboard 'CI Runners': queue depth, disk usage, agent status.
- Alert `runner-disk-usage` pages Cloud on-call at 80% root volume.

## Known failure modes
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| All runners offline, agent log 'no space left on device' | Docker layer cache fills the 100 GB root volume (June 2026 incident) | `sudo docker system prune -af`, then `sudo systemctl restart actions.runner.*`. Nightly prune timer should prevent this - check `systemctl list-timers` |
| Single runner offline after reboot | Agent not registered after instance replacement | Re-run the registration script from the AMI user-data; token from the org settings |
| Jobs queued but runners idle | Label mismatch in workflow `runs-on` | Compare labels in workflow vs runner settings |

## AMI rebuild checklist
1. Base on the latest Ubuntu 24.04 golden image.
2. Include: Docker, runner agent, Datadog agent, **nightly prune timer (`docker-prune.timer`)**, CloudWatch agent.
3. Bake, test on runner-prod-4 first, then roll the others one at a time outside working hours.
4. Update the AMI ID in `algoworks-infra/ci/runners.tf` via PR; keep the previous AMI ID for rollback.

## Escalation
Cloud on-call (PagerDuty schedule 'Cloud Infrastructure'), then Varun Chandra.

title: Runbook: GlobalProtect VPN - certificate renewal and outage response
body:
**Owner:** Identity & Access Management | **Created:** 4 June 2026 (Lakshmi Narayanan) after INC-22005

2. Submit the CSR in the DigiCert portal (credentials in 1Password vault 'IAM-Infra').
3. Import the issued certificate and chain on **both** gateways; set as the portal and gateway SSL/TLS profile certificate.

- Symptom: all remote users see 'Portal certificate is invalid'. Office LAN users are unaffected.

title: ADR-014: v4 public API protocol - REST/OpenAPI-first; gRPC internal only
body:
**Status:** Accepted (20 January 2026) | **Deciders:** Rohan Mehta, Sneha Kulkarni, Priya Shah, Arjun Venkataraman | **Project:** PROJ-01

## Context
The v3 monolith exposes ~180 REST endpoints with inconsistent contracts and no machine-readable spec. Customers integrate with the API directly (34 enterprise customers have custom integrations). For v4 we needed to choose the external protocol and how strictly to manage contracts.

## Options considered
1. **REST + OpenAPI-first** (spec is the source of truth; server stubs, clients and contract tests generated).
2. **gRPC externally with a REST transcoding gateway.**
3. **GraphQL** for the portal with REST retained for integrations.

## Decision
Option 1 for the public API. gRPC is adopted **only** for internal service-to-service calls behind the gateway, phased in after GA. GraphQL is not pursued.

## Rationale
- Customer integrations are REST/JSON; a protocol change would reset the 12-month migration clock.
- OpenAPI-first gives us contract tests in CI (blocking breaking changes) and generated SDKs for the portal and mobile apps.
- gRPC's benefits (streaming, binary efficiency) matter most for telematics ingest, which is internal.

## Consequences
- `algoworks-api-v4` repo adopts spec-first workflow; PRs that change `openapi.yaml` require two approvals (data-pipeline rule extended).
- Sneha Kulkarni owns the contract-test harness (PLAT-2150).
- Gateway keeps v3 compatibility routes for 12 months from GA.
- Revisit gRPC-external in Q2 2027 if a customer requires streaming.

title: ADR-011: Multi-region topology - warm standby in ap-southeast-1 (active-passive)
body:
**Status:** Accepted (10 November 2025) | **Deciders:** Varun Chandra, Sandeep Malhotra; consulted Rohan Mehta, Vivek Anand | **Project:** PROJ-02

## Context
Two APAC prospects (Singapore, Malaysia) require data residency in the region and a documented DR capability; our current RTO from a single-region loss is 'rebuild from backups' (~6 hours).

## Options
| Option | RTO | Monthly run-rate (est.) | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Backup/restore only (status quo) | ~6h | USD 0 | low |
| B. **Warm standby (active-passive)**: replica DB, pre-built EKS, apps synced but scaled to zero, Route 53 failover | ~30 min | ~USD 9,000 | medium |
| C. Active-active with global load balancing and multi-writer DB | ~0 | ~USD 22,000 | high (data consistency for telematics writes) |

## Decision
**Option B.** Singapore is a warm standby with cross-region RDS replication (async), EKS pre-provisioned, ArgoCD applications synced with replicas=0, and Route 53 health-check failover. Failover is a documented manual runbook (promote replica, scale apps, flip DNS) targeting 30 minutes.

## Consequences
- Meets residency by allowing APAC tenants to be pinned to the Singapore region in phase 2 (Q3 2026).
- Monitoring must distinguish standby from active (see incident of May 2026 for what happens otherwise).
- Quarterly failover drill required; first drill March 2026.
- FP&A tracks the run-rate as a separate cost line.

title: Driver App Offline Mode - design decision: local queue and last-write-wins conflict resolution
body:
**Date:** 22 September 2025 | **Authors:** Farhan Siddiqui, Vikram Nair | **Approved:** Meera Krishnan | **Project:** PROJ-04

## Problem
Drivers lose connectivity in warehouses and rural routes; check-ins and proof-of-delivery captured offline must reach the platform reliably and in order, and conflicts must be resolved predictably.

## Decision
1. **Local queue:** SQLite (Room on Android, GRDB on iOS) event table with monotonically increasing sequence numbers per device.
2. **Sync:** background job replays events in order over the v3 batch endpoint (v4 later); at-least-once with server-side idempotency key = deviceId + sequence.
3. **Conflict resolution:** **last-write-wins by device timestamp** for the same trip field. The server keeps an audit row of the overwritten value (`trip_event_audit`) so support can see what was replaced.
4. Photos (POD) are uploaded after events, with retry; the event references the photo by local id until upload completes.

## Alternatives rejected
- CRDT / field-level merge: correct but heavy; conflicts are rare (one driver per trip in 99.6% of trips).
- Server-wins: loses legitimate offline edits.

## Risks
- Device clock skew -> server compares against receive time when skew > 5 minutes and flags the trip.
- Large queues after long offline periods -> batch size 200, progress UI.

Shipped in Driver App 3.5 (January 2026).

title: Decision: GitOps pull-request approval as the change record for application deployments
body:
**Date:** 25 August 2025 (proposed), 2 September 2025 (approved at CAB) | **Owner:** Varun Chandra | **Project:** PROJ-06 | **CAB record:** CHG-20783

## Context
Under the Change Management Policy (v2) every production application deployment needs a CHG reviewed at the twice-weekly CAB. With Jenkins this was tolerable (2-3 deploys/week). ArgoCD enables 10-20 deploys/day; CAB would become the bottleneck and CHG records would be rubber-stamped.

## Decision
From ArgoCD go-live (1 December 2025):
- **Standard application deployment** = a change to an existing service's image tag, replica count, resource limits, or feature-flag config in `algoworks-deploy`. Approval = merged PR with required CODEOWNER review and green CI. **No CHG, no CAB.** ArgoCD's sync history plus the PR is the audit trail.
- **Still CAB / CHG:** Terraform/infrastructure, network and firewall, Okta and identity configuration, database schema or parameter changes, new services or new external endpoints, anything touching secrets management.
- **Emergency changes:** unchanged (verbal approval by Cloud Infra Lead, retrospective CHG).

## Open question (raised at CAB, not resolved)
Whether config-only changes with high blast radius (connection pools, timeouts, rate limits) should carry a `high-risk-config` label requiring an extra reviewer. Revisit after 3 months. (See the March 2026 postmortem, action item 3.)

## Follow-ups
- Update the Change Management Policy with a 'GitOps standard deployment' category - **owner Varun Chandra, due October 2025.**
- Engineering onboarding guide to explain what does and doesn't need a CHG.

title: ServiceNow Self-Service Catalog - access request routing design (decision, 19 May 2026)
body:
**Project:** PROJ-07 | **Decided by:** Rajesh Kumar, Nikhil Bhatt | **Built by:** Shruti Joshi

## Problem
60% of 'access' tickets arrive as free-text incidents with no approver named, so IAM chases approvals by Slack. The Application Access Request Policy requires a recorded line-manager approval and, for admin roles, the owning team lead.

## Design
1. One catalog item per application (wave 1: Salesforce, Zendesk, HubSpot, Metabase, GitHub; wave 2: VPN, shared mailbox, laptop, software install, contractor account).
2. **Approval step 1:** line manager, auto-populated from the Darwinbox -> ServiceNow user sync. If the manager has a Darwinbox delegate set, the delegate is used. *Escalation when the manager is unavailable follows the policy (Department Head); the catalog does not auto-approve.*
3. **Approval step 2 (admin roles only):** owning team lead from the Systems Directory mapping table (`u_system_owner`).
4. **Fulfilment:** RITM assigned to IAM for the Okta group; sub-task to the system administrator for in-app role.
5. Training prerequisites (e.g. Admin Console) are a checkbox the requester attests and IAM verifies.

## Decisions
- Do not build auto-approval on SLA breach (discussed and rejected: not in policy).
- Role bundles from the Darwinbox onboarding automation remain separate from the catalog; new joiners still use catalog items for anything outside their bundle.

## Metrics
Target: 80% of access requests via catalog by September 2026; median time-to-approve under 2 business days.

title: Zoho Expense -> NetSuite integration: posting design decision (9 June 2026)
body:
**Project:** PROJ-18 | **Decided by:** Shalini Menon, Ashwin Raman | **Built by:** Manish Tiwari (Data Eng, embedded) with Payal Shah

## Decision
Post **one summarised journal entry per day**, with lines grouped by cost centre x expense category x GST rate, instead of one journal line per expense claim. Expense-level detail stays in Zoho Expense; each NetSuite journal carries a `zoho_batch_id` and a drill-back URL for auditors.

## Why
- ~1,100 expense lines/month would make NetSuite journals unwieldy and slow the close.
- Auditors have accepted summarised posting with drill-back (confirmed with the statutory auditors 2 June).
- Reimbursement payouts remain in Keka payroll; NetSuite needs the accrual, not the individual claim.

## Mechanics
- Daily at 02:00 IST the integration pulls approved claims since the last batch, aggregates, and posts via NetSuite REST (custom record `ZohoBatchLog` records batch id, totals, status).
- Reversals in Zoho generate a negative line in the next batch.
- Failure -> alert to #finance and retry next run. *(Retry behaviour revised after the August 2026 duplicate incident: idempotency key required - see INC-22375.)*

## Go-live
Parallel run June (manual upload continues); automated posting only from 1 July 2026.

title: Okta SSO - user guide
body:
**System ID:** SYS-10 | **Owner team:** Identity & Access Management | **Criticality:** critical | **Category:** internal | **Updated:** 2026-05-06

## What it is
Identity provider for all SaaS and internal apps. Enforces MFA (Okta Verify push / FIDO2). Source of truth for app assignments via groups. Phase 2 rollout (2025) moved Salesforce, Zendesk, HubSpot and Darwinbox to SSO-only.

## How to get access
Every employee gets an Okta account on Day -1 via the Darwinbox -> Okta HR-driven provisioning flow. Application assignments are driven by Okta group membership; group changes are requested via ServiceNow and fulfilled by IAM.

## Common tasks
- Log in at algoworks.okta.com; every app tile you are assigned appears on the dashboard.
- Enrol a second factor (Touch ID / Windows Hello or a security key) under Settings > Security Methods so you can self-service resets.
- Group-based app assignment: if an app tile is missing, you need the Okta group - request via the ServiceNow access catalog, not Slack.
- Admins: app configuration changes (SAML settings, attribute mappings) are Normal changes - raise a CHG.

## Known issues and gotchas
- Push notifications not arriving: check the phone's automatic time setting before re-enrolling.
- New joiners see only the default bundle plus their role bundle on Day 1; anything else is a catalog request.
- During an Okta vendor outage nothing behind SSO works, including ServiceNow and Slack - the office WhatsApp group is the fallback channel.

## Support
IAM queue in ServiceNow; urgent lockouts by phone to the Service Desk (ext. 200).

title: GlobalProtect VPN - user guide
body:

Palo Alto GlobalProtect remote-access VPN. Required for the AlgoWorks Admin Console, Metabase, Snowflake private link, internal Confluence spaces flagged 'restricted' and the office file shares. Split-tunnel by default.

## How to get access
Request via ServiceNow 'VPN access' catalog item with manager approval. IAM adds the user to the appropriate Okta VPN group. Contractors receive VPN through a sponsored account and must be explicitly scoped.

## Common tasks
- Install GlobalProtect from the Company Portal; portal address vpn.algoworks.io; sign in with Okta.
- Needed for: AlgoWorks Admin Console, Metabase, Snowflake private link, restricted Confluence spaces, office file shares.
- Split tunnel is the default; request the full-tunnel profile only for travel to high-risk locations.
- Employee VPN membership is via the vpn-employees Okta group and renews automatically while you are an active employee.

## Known issues and gotchas
- 'Portal certificate is invalid' for everyone remote = expired certificate; see the certificate runbook.
- Connects then drops after ~20 seconds on some home routers: MTU issue - IAM can push a lower MTU for your gateway profile.
- Periodic disconnects every ~30 minutes on home Wi-Fi: under investigation as a problem record (rekey suspected); collect logs when it happens.

IAM queue; gateway outages are Sev2 - post in #incidents.

**Owner:** Engineering (Rohan Mehta) | **Updated:** 24 July 2026

## Week one

## How we ship
- Merge to `main` with a CODEOWNER review and green CI. Promote via a PR in `algoworks-deploy`; ArgoCD does the rest.
- **Do I need a CHG?** For a standard application deployment (image tag, replicas, resources, feature-flag config of an existing service): **no** - the merged algoworks-deploy PR is the approval (CAB decision, September 2025). For Terraform/infrastructure, network, Okta configuration, database schema or parameters, new services or new external endpoints: **yes**, raise a CHG for the Tuesday/Thursday CAB. *The Change Management Policy page has not yet been updated to say this; the rule here is the operating one.*
- **Fridays:** deployments allowed before 14:00 IST if behind a feature flag or trivially reversible; stay online until 16:00. Month-end billing freeze (last two business days) still applies. Mobile releases follow the 48-hour internal-track soak.
- Pool/limit/timeout changes: separate PR with the `high-risk-config` label and a second reviewer.

## Environments
Sandbox (yours), staging (refreshed from prod snapshots Sundays), production (read-only; elevated access is a 4-hour break-glass session with Cloud Lead approval).

Code: GitHub algoworks-tech. Work: Jira PLAT/FE/DATA. Docs: this space. Chat: #eng-platform, #eng-frontend, #eng-data, #devops-sre, #incidents.

title: How to report a security incident or a phishing email
body:
**Owner:** IAM & Security (Amit Saxena) | **Updated:** 4 May 2026 | **Classification:** Internal

## Phishing or suspicious email
Click **Report Phish** in Outlook (desktop, web and mobile). That is all you need to do; Security sees it within minutes. If you clicked a link or entered your password: call the Service Desk (ext. 200) immediately - you will not be in trouble, and speed matters far more than embarrassment.

## Other security incidents
Lost or stolen laptop/phone, credentials shared by mistake, suspected account compromise, data sent to the wrong recipient, unusual system behaviour: post in **#security** (private - ask to be added) or call the Service Desk out of hours. Do not investigate on your own.

## What happens next
Security classifies the incident (Incident Management SOP severities apply; a credential compromise is P1), contains it (sessions revoked, factors reset, devices wiped where needed), and follows up with you. Postmortems are blameless.

## Reminders
- AlgoWorks never asks for passwords or bank changes by email; vendor bank changes go through Finance AP with a call-back.
- Credentials belong in 1Password shared vaults, never in Slack, email or documents.
- Quarterly phishing simulations run under the Security Awareness programme; clicking one leads to a short refresher, nothing else.

body:
**Owner:** IT Service Desk | **Updated:** 30 June 2026

## Before you leave the office
Install from the Company Portal: GlobalProtect, Okta Verify (phone), 1Password, Slack, Zoom. Test the VPN once from the office guest network.

Lock your screen, do not use public Wi-Fi without VPN, report lost devices immediately. Restricted data (payroll, contracts, customer PII) must not be downloaded to personal devices or printed at home.

The office does not reimburse home monitors or chairs (Hybrid Work Policy). Designated remote employees may request a monitor from the Service Desk (shipped once). Connectivity allowances are decided by Finance - check with Finance AP for the current position.

Core collaboration hours 11:00-16:00 IST. Singapore and US staff overlap at least 3 hours; use the Outlook scheduling assistant.
